fixes.explanation: Not quite. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." (Amos 7:3) Then He says, "It will not happen…" The locust plan does not go ahead. Amos asked, and the LORD answered.
False is right. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." (Amos 7:3) Then He says, "It will not happen…" The locust plan does not go ahead. Amos speaks, and the LORD relents.
Running home isn't in the text. Amos says, "Lord GOD, please stop!" (Amos 7:5) I'd have been halfway to the door, honestly. Amos speaks up for Jacob instead.

It will not happen either. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." Then the Lord GOD says, "It will not happen either…" (Amos 7:6) The word "either" matters. It's the second time the LORD relents after Amos speaks.

Gath is a swing and a miss. The Lord says, "I am setting a plumb line among My people Israel…" (Amos 7:8) He says "My people," so this one isn't about outsiders. I think that makes it hit closer to home.
Deserted. The Lord says, "The high places of Isaac will be deserted…" (Amos 7:9) They'll sit empty, like a bakery with the lights off and nobody inside.

Crowded is the opposite of what the Lord says. "The high places of Isaac will be deserted…" (Amos 7:9) Crowded would be a packed house, and this is an empty one. Nobody's showing up, not even somebody pretending to be busy.

Sword. The Lord says, "…I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword." (Amos 7:9) Watch how it gets personal. First the high places, then the sanctuaries, and now a house with a name on it.
A staff sounds gentler, but that isn't the word. The Lord says, "…I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword." (Amos 7:9) It's a sword, and it's aimed at the house of Jeroboam.
